name: Rinnemann's Green
lede: Rinnemann's Green is a soft, mid-toned green dated to about 1794 in Maerz and Paul's dictionary, and no book we hold explains whom it was named for.

sections.title: A name the books leave open
sections.body:
Ridgway placed this green on plate XVIII of his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 carries it as block 120 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates the name to about 1794, decades before either standard, on their plate 20 [1]. Who Rinnemann was is undocumented in the sources we hold, and Ridgway drew his thousands of named samples from many older lists rather than coining every name himself [1][2].

Its nearest library neighbors are [[chromium-green|Chromium Green]] and [[russian-green|Russian Green]], with [[grey-green|Grey Green]] close behind, and it reads greyer than the everyday [[moss]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Measured in LCH terms it sits at lightness 57, chroma 27, hue 130 degrees [3]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, it appears 169 times, about 0.7 percent, including in Julian Alden Weir's 1908 landscape *Obweebetuck* and Van Gogh's 1887 *Fishing in Spring, the Pont de Clichy* [4]. These are computed color matches on aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [4].
